title: Take out the trash
briefing: A leftover build directory is wasting space. Delete it — all of it.
Remember: rm has no undo and no recycle bin. Read before you press Enter.
tips: `rm FILE` deletes a file. A directory with contents needs `rm -r` (recursive).
objective: Delete the entire ~/build directory and everything inside it.
hints: `rm` on a directory complains — a directory isn't a single file.
To remove a directory and everything in it, rm needs to go recursive: the -r flag.

reactions.say: If rm complained 'Is a directory', that's expected — a directory needs `rm -r` to remove it and its contents.

explanation: `rm -r` removes a directory and everything inside, recursively. There is no trash can — deleted is deleted. The safety habit: run `ls` on what you're about to delete first, and never, ever `rm -rf /` (the game refuses it, real machines don't).
